contradiction_resolution: No claim-level contradiction: contradicts_claim_ids is empty, and the statement does not oppose CONJ-0001, THM-0001-THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. It is compatible with THM-0001 (stack versus space conventions) and THM-0005 (c(6)=5, so n=6 needs residual geometry). INDEPENDENT CHECKS. (1) Inertia of a scheme or algebraic space is trivial: Stacks Proposition 94.13.3 (04SZ) says an algebraic stack is an algebraic space if and only if I_X -> X is an equivalence; Stacks 04XA records that a roman-capital algebraic stack is required to have trivial inertia. If B is a reduced locally Noetherian k-scheme, as ATT-0089 theorem_statement declares, then C->B is a scheme morphism, Hilb^6(C/B) and Pic^6(C/B) are algebraic spaces, and I is an algebraic space, so Aut of a geometric point of I is 1 and 1->Aut(x_tilde)->Aut(x)->S_6 degenerates to 1->1->1->S_6. (2) I is defined from Hilb^6 and Pic^6 only; gamma enters only in the construction of L, not as part of an object of I. ATT-0089 step 4 ('an ordered automorphism induces a PGL_2 transformation fixing the three images') therefore requires Aut to mean Aut(C,gamma,Gamma). Vakil Class 35 records that Aut(P^1) is three-transitive, so a PGL_2 element fixing three distinct points is the identity; that step is correct for the cover group and unavailable for Aut(C,Gamma). (3) A geometric point of M_{6,6} has automorphism group Aut(C; p_1,...,p_6)=Aut(C,Gamma) (ordered or unordered), so that is the group relevant to the forgetful map. (4) Kernel triviality is not formal. Stacks Lemma 53.12.2 (0C1D) gives 2g-2 = deg(f)(2g_Y-2)+deg(R). For the hyperelliptic involution, deg(f)=2 and g_Y=0, hence deg(R)=2g+2. Vakil Class 35 states that a hyperelliptic cover has precisely 2g+2 distinct branch points; in characteristic not 2 each branch point has a unique ramification point, so the involution fixes 2g+2=14 points on a genus-6 curve and can therefore fix six marked points. Fujimori (Ann. Scuola Norm. Sup. Pisa 1997) records the same 2g+2 upper bound for any non-identity automorphism of a curve of genus g>=2. SCOPE. The 2g+2 witness is hyperelliptic, and FND-0125 excludes hyperelliptic composed degree-4 pencils from the balanced CE locus, so this is a formal obstruction rather than a point of the campaign family. Complementary to corroborated FND-0098 (mono into M_{6,6} requires recovering gamma from L, plus a stack-level Aut argument), FND-0127 (scheme-versus-stack base scope for Grauert/H3), FND-0075 (S_6-torsor at stack level, not on coarse moduli), and FND-0060 (Hurwitz coarse dimension needs stabilizer bookkeeping). Distinct from pending FND-0138, which is the positive B_3 repair Aut(C,Gamma)=Aut(C,gamma,Gamma), not this well-posedness obstruction. Not a merge into FND-0098, FND-0101, or FND-0127: those concern monomorphism of Z, gap-marker discipline, and projective-bundle descent respectively. Promote candidate to corroborated; evidence_class upgraded from adversarial_review to primary_source. The finding's sole reviewer_engine (claude) is in this revision's excluded_engines; this audit is the first non-excluded verification.

scope.exact_mathematical_scope: Any inertia/stabilizer clause 1->Aut(x_tilde)->Aut(x)->S_6 for a geometric point x of the Abel-Jacobi incidence I=Hilb^6(C/B) x_{Pic^6(C/B)} B is well-posed only after the stack and the moduli problem defining Aut are named. If B is a scheme, then I is an algebraic space, so its inertia is trivial and the sequence is 1->1->1->S_6: exact but vacuous. Over a stack base Aut(x) is the automorphism group of the object classified by that base. A rigidity argument that produces an induced PGL_2 element of P^1 fixing three marked images applies only to Aut(C,gamma,Gamma). It does not by itself prove the corresponding statement for Aut(C,Gamma), which is the inertia group of a geometric point of M_{6,6}. Kernel triviality for Aut(C;p_1,...,p_6) is not formal: a non-identity automorphism of a smooth genus-6 curve can fix as many as 2g+2=14 points and therefore can fix six marked points.
